An adapter can implement a stable atomic slot to own the whole interaction of one control. This page
lists, for each slot, the exact props type, the root element, the `pt` parts, whether a ref is
forwarded and which behavior stays in Components. It is generated from the profiles that
`@cratis/components.conformance` runs against a declared slot, so it describes what is tested. See
[Primitive adaptation profile](primitive-adaptation.md#stable-atomic-slots) for how a library
declares an atomic slot.

## `datatables.paginator`

| Contract | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Props | `TablePaginatorProps` |
| Root element | `<div>` matching `[role="navigation"]` |
| Parts | `root`, `range`, `info`, `pages`, `page`, `ellipsis`, `first`, `previous`, `next`, `last` |
| Ref | None; the slot does not forward a ref |

Components owns:

- The props contract: zero-based `page`, `pageCount`, zero-based `onPageChange` and the optional range and label props
- The paging state that supplies those props
- The built-in paginator, used whenever the slot is not declared

The adapter owns:

- The navigation controls, their keyboard activation and their focus behavior
- Calling `onPageChange` with the zero-based target page, converting at the boundary when the design system counts from one

```tsx
import type { TablePaginatorProps } from '@cratis/components/DataTables';
import type { CratisAtomicSlotMap } from '@cratis/components/renderer';

const ExamplePaginator = ({ page, pageCount, onPageChange, pt }: TablePaginatorProps) => (
    <div {...pt?.root} role='navigation' aria-label='Pagination' data-cratis-part='root'>
        <button
            type='button'
            aria-label='Previous page'
            disabled={page === 0}
            data-cratis-part='previous'
            onClick={() => onPageChange(page - 1)}
        >
            Previous
        </button>
        <span {...pt?.info} data-cratis-part='info'>
            {page + 1} / {pageCount}
        </span>
        <button
            type='button'
            aria-label='Next page'
            disabled={page >= pageCount - 1}
            data-cratis-part='next'
            onClick={() => onPageChange(page + 1)}
        >
            Next
        </button>
    </div>
);

export const atomicSlots = {
    'datatables.paginator': { mode: 'atomic', fidelity: 'native', render: ExamplePaginator },
} satisfies CratisAtomicSlotMap;
```

## `common.tooltip`

| Contract | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Props | `TooltipProps` |
| Root element | `<button>` matching `[data-cratis-part="trigger"]` |
| Parts | None in `pt` |
| Ref | None; the slot does not forward a ref |

Components owns:

- The props contract: non-interactive `content`, `position`, `disabled`, `className` and exactly one focusable trigger child
- The overlay host and overlay container that the popup is bound to, read through `unstable_useOverlayHost()` and `unstable_useOverlayEnvironment()`

The adapter owns:

- The trigger and popup parts, and describing the trigger with `aria-describedby` only
- Opening on hover and keyboard focus, and closing on blur and Escape
- Closing immediately when the overlay host closes, unmounts or changes

```tsx
import { cloneElement } from 'react';
import type { TooltipProps } from '@cratis/components/Common';
import type { CratisAtomicSlotMap } from '@cratis/components/renderer';

const ExampleTooltip = ({ content, disabled, children }: TooltipProps) => {
    if (disabled || !content) {
        return children;
    }
    return (
        <>
            {cloneElement(children, {
                'data-cratis-part': children.props['data-cratis-part'] ?? 'trigger',
            })}
            <div role='tooltip' data-cratis-part='popup' data-open>
                {content}
            </div>
        </>
    );
};

export const atomicSlots = {
    'common.tooltip': { mode: 'atomic', fidelity: 'native', render: ExampleTooltip },
} satisfies CratisAtomicSlotMap;
```

## `dropdown.select`

| Contract | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Props | `DropdownProps<unknown>` |
| Root element | `<button>` matching `[data-cratis-part="trigger"]` |
| Parts | `root`, `value`, `filter`, `trigger`, `clear`, `popover`, `listbox`, `option`, `multiple`, `indicator` |
| Ref | None; the slot does not forward a ref |

Components owns:

- The props contract: `value`, `options`, `onChange` and the `multiple`, `filter` and `showClear` modes
- The overlay container the popover renders into

The adapter owns:

- The trigger, filter input, listbox and options, with one keyboard and focus owner
- Opening, arrow-key and Enter selection, and Escape to close
- Calling `onChange` once per user selection with `source: 'user'` and the native event

```tsx
import type { DropdownProps } from '@cratis/components/Dropdown';
import type { CratisAtomicSlotMap } from '@cratis/components/renderer';

const ExampleSelect = ({ disabled, pt }: DropdownProps<unknown>) => (
    <div {...pt?.root} data-cratis-part='root'>
        <button type='button' aria-haspopup='listbox' disabled={disabled} data-cratis-part='trigger'>
            Choose
        </button>
    </div>
);

export const atomicSlots = {
    'dropdown.select': { mode: 'atomic', fidelity: 'native', render: ExampleSelect },
} satisfies CratisAtomicSlotMap;
```

## `display.datePicker`

| Contract | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Props | `DatePickerInputProps` |
| Root element | `<div>` matching `[data-cratis-part="group"]` |
| Parts | `root`, `group`, `input`, `segment`, `placeholder`, `trigger`, `popover`, `dialog`, `calendar`, `header`, `previous`, `heading`, `next`, `grid`, `cell`, `buttonBar`, `today`, `clear` |
| Ref | None; the slot does not forward a ref |

Components owns:

- The props contract: a `Date` or `null` value, `minDate`, `maxDate`, `disabled`, `readOnly` and `invalid`
- The overlay container the popover renders into

The adapter owns:

- The segmented input and the calendar popover, with one keyboard and focus owner
- Calling `onChange` once per user selection with `source: 'user'` and the native event
- Keeping the value type of its calendar library inside the adapter

```tsx
import type { DatePickerInputProps } from '@cratis/components/Common';
import type { CratisAtomicSlotMap } from '@cratis/components/renderer';

const ExampleDatePicker = ({ disabled, pt }: DatePickerInputProps) => (
    <div {...pt?.group} role='group' data-cratis-part='group'>
        <input {...pt?.input} disabled={disabled} data-cratis-part='input' />
        <button type='button' aria-label='Open calendar' disabled={disabled} data-cratis-part='trigger' />
    </div>
);

export const atomicSlots = {
    'display.datePicker': { mode: 'atomic', fidelity: 'native', render: ExampleDatePicker },
} satisfies CratisAtomicSlotMap;
```

## `dialogs.dialog`

| Contract | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Props | `CratisDialogSlotProps` |
| Root element | `<section>` matching `[role="dialog"]`, or a platform `<dialog>` |
| Parts | `backdrop`, `positioner`, `root`, `header`, `title`, `subtitle`, `headerActions`, `close`, `content`, `footer`, `confirm`, `cancel`. A platform `<dialog>` owns `backdrop` and `positioner`, so those two parts then have no element |
| Ref | None; the slot does not forward a ref |

Components owns:

- The dialog stack tier and z-index, and the `DialogResult` flow
- The typed footer and its buttons, the header actions, busy and validity state, and the announcement live region
- Initial focus, and the overlay environment that descendants portal into

The adapter owns:

- The modal shell: focus trap, Escape, outside press, scroll lock and focus restoration
- The header, title, subtitle and close button, rendered from the props and the `host` prop

```tsx
import type { HTMLAttributes } from 'react';
import type { CratisDialogSlotProps } from '@cratis/components/Dialogs';
import type { CratisAtomicSlotMap } from '@cratis/components/renderer';

const ExampleDialog = ({ title, pt, host }: CratisDialogSlotProps) => (
    <dialog
        {...(pt?.root as HTMLAttributes<HTMLDialogElement> | undefined)}
        open
        aria-labelledby={`${host.id}-title`}
        data-cratis-part='root'
        data-open
    >
        <h2 id={`${host.id}-title`} ref={host.titleRef} data-cratis-part='title'>
            {title}
        </h2>
        <button
            type='button'
            aria-label={host.closeAriaLabel}
            data-cratis-part='close'
            onClick={() => host.dismiss('closeButton')}
        >
            {host.closeIcon}
        </button>
        {host.content}
        {host.footer}
        <div ref={host.registerOverlayContainer} />
    </dialog>
);

export const atomicSlots = {
    'dialogs.dialog': { mode: 'atomic', fidelity: 'native', render: ExampleDialog },
} satisfies CratisAtomicSlotMap;
```

## `common.numberInput`

| Contract | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Props | `NumericInputProps` |
| Root element | `<input>` matching `input[type="number"]` |
| Parts | `root` |
| Ref | Forwards a ref to the root element |

Components owns:

- The props contract: a controlled numeric `value`, `invalid`, native input attributes and `onChange`
- Converting an `undefined` change into the command value

The adapter owns:

- The native number input and its typing interaction
- Reporting the next number, or `undefined` when the input is empty or not a valid number

```tsx
import { forwardRef } from 'react';
import type { NumericInputProps } from '@cratis/components/Common';
import type { CratisAtomicSlotMap } from '@cratis/components/renderer';

const ExampleNumberInput = forwardRef<HTMLInputElement, NumericInputProps>(
    function ExampleNumberInput({ value, invalid, onChange, pt, ...inputProps }, ref) {
        return (
            <input
                {...inputProps}
                {...pt?.root}
                ref={ref}
                type='number'
                value={value ?? ''}
                aria-invalid={invalid || undefined}
                data-cratis-part='root'
                onChange={(event) => {
                    const next = event.currentTarget.valueAsNumber;
                    onChange?.(Number.isNaN(next) ? undefined : next);
                }}
            />
        );
    },
);

export const atomicSlots = {
    'common.numberInput': { mode: 'atomic', fidelity: 'native', render: ExampleNumberInput },
} satisfies CratisAtomicSlotMap;
```
